items.title: Tencent open-sources Hy4: 770B total, 49B active per token
items.summary: Tencent's Hy Team released weights for Hy4, a new-generation MoE flagship that handles text, image and video understanding with a 1M context length, alongside Hy4-FP8 and the pre-trained base model. The model card says Hy4 ranks first among open-weight models across 579 real-world financial tasks, while acknowledging a notable gap to top proprietary models. It ships under the Tencent Hy License, so check the terms before commercial use; teams that self-host long-context models get another open-weight option.

evidence.quote: Hy4 is a new-generation Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) flagship model developed by the Tencent Hy Team, supporting text, image, and video understanding. The language backbone comprises 770B total parameters, of which 49B are activated per token.
Context Length 1M (1,048,576 tokens)
Across 579 real-world financial tasks, Hy4 ranks first among open-weight models
a notable gap remains between it and top proprietary models
We open-source Hy4 , Hy4-FP8 , and the pre-trained Hy4 base model weights on Hugging Face
Hy4 is released under the Tencent Hy License

items.title: Apple releases Depth Pro 2 for metric depth on images and video
items.summary: Apple's machine learning research team released Depth Pro 2, which estimates the depth of every pixel in meters from ordinary camera photos, videos or live feeds at full input resolution. The authors say prior methods trade temporal consistency against boundary sharpness, and that Depth Pro 2 is metrically accurate, sharp and temporally consistent all at once; code and weights from 24M to 872M parameters are available. The weights use the Apple Machine Learning Research Model license for non-commercial research only, and smaller sizes run faster while larger ones give sharper, steadier depth.

evidence.quote: Depth Pro 2 estimates the depth of every pixel, in meters, from images taken with an ordinary camera.
multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness
Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions.
We release code and weights here
S apple/DepthPro2-S 24M 97 MB B apple/DepthPro2-B 97M 386 MB L apple/DepthPro2-L 334M 1.3 GB H+ apple/DepthPro2-H 872M 3.5 GB
The weights are released under the Apple Machine Learning Research Model license , for research use only: non-commercial scientific research and academic development.

items.title: pi-H3 brings MiniMax H3 audio-video generation down to 2–4 steps
items.summary: Researchers from Stanford University released pi-H3, 2-step and 4-step adapters for MiniMax H3 that combine pi-Flow v2 few-step distillation with DWD (Decoding Without a Decoder), predicting video frames directly at the last step so the video skips the VAE decoder. The authors call it the fastest way to generate MiniMax H3 videos with synchronized audio; the adapters support text, first-frame and last-frame conditioning, INT8 versions are provided for ComfyUI, and use is governed by the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement.

evidence.quote: 2-step and 4-step adapters of MiniMax H3 , the fastest way to generate MiniMax H3 videos with synchronized audio. pi-H3 combines pi-Flow v2 few-step distillation with DWD (Decoding Without a Decoder), which predicts the video frames directly at the last step, so the video skips the VAE decoder.
All adapters support text, first-frame, and last-frame conditioning. We recommend the DWD adapters. The INT8 ConvRot versions are for ComfyUI only.
The pi-H3 adapters are Model Derivatives of MiniMax H3 and are distributed under the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement

items.title: InclusionMed benchmarks medical AI by role and capability
items.summary: InclusionMed is an open medical AI evaluation initiative whose first release selected four public benchmarks from 388 candidates and adds a private diagnostic reasoning benchmark, InclusionMed-DxFiles. Frontier LLMs scored from 17.5 to 49.1 out of 100, ranks shifted with the healthcare role or capability, and the ten highest-ranked models all did better on patient communication than on clinical decision-making. Developers building medical apps should pick models for their specific setting, since models with similar scores also differed substantially in estimated inference cost.

evidence.quote: For the first release, we selected four public benchmarks from 388 candidates through structured audits and independent reproduction.
with overall scores ranging from 17.5 to 49.1 out of 100

items.title: VibePrevisBench tests coding agents building 4D scenes in Blender
items.summary: VibePrevisBench asks an agent to turn a brief into an executable 4D scene in Blender and render its proxy video, with 242 tasks spanning scripts, photos, continuations and reference videos, scored by a rule-based Scene Check and a VLM-based Screen Check. Analyzing 11 frontier coding agents, the authors find multimodal understanding of space and camera motion separates them, and that agents inspect their own renders but fail to correct their errors. For builders of creative-tool agents, item-by-item verification of renders against the brief is the current weak spot.

evidence.quote: Its 242 tasks span four input kinds, including scripts, photos, continuations, and reference videos.
We analyze the evaluation results and trajectories of 11 frontier coding agents and identify three key observations.
Third, agents inspect their own renders but fail to correct their errors.

items.title: AscendGYM benchmarks agents optimizing kernels on Ascend NPUs
items.summary: AscendGYM is a kernel optimization benchmark for Ascend NPUs whose initial suite has 48 kernels across three difficulty levels, with test cases whose data types and tensor shapes come from real training and inference tasks. It also proposes the Speedup-Token Score (STS), which measures performance gains relative to token cost. Teams optimizing training or inference on Ascend can use it to gauge what a coding agent achieves within a budget.

evidence.quote: we introduce AscendGYM, a benchmark whose initial suite comprises 48 kernels across three difficulty levels. Each kernel is paired with test cases whose data types and tensor shapes are collected from real-world training and inference tasks.
we propose a new metric, the Speedup-Token Score (STS) , which quantifies performance gains relative to token cost

items.title: Transformers v5.24.0 adds Inkling 2 Mini, Apertus 1.5 and Dory
items.summary: Hugging Face Transformers v5.24.0 adds Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling 2 Mini (layers 6 to 17 run three times), the Swiss AI Initiative's multimodal Apertus 1.5 with its WavTokenizer audio tokenizer, NVIDIA's looped language model Dory, HY4-VL, and Meta FAIR's Omnilingual ASR covering more than 1,600 languages. Dory's loop count can be changed at inference time on the same checkpoint to trade speed against quality; after upgrading, these models load directly in Transformers.

evidence.quote: Apertus 1.5 is a multimodal model from the Swiss AI Initiative that accepts text, images and audio and generates text.
Dory is a looped (latent-recurrent) language model from NVIDIA.
The loop count can be changed at inference time on the same checkpoint to trade speed against quality.
HY4-VL (Hunyuan V4 Vision-Language) combines the HYV4 mixture-of-experts text backbone with a vision encoder for image-text and video-text generation.
Omnilingual ASR is a suite of multilingual speech-recognition models from Meta FAIR that covers more than 1,600 languages.
The 40-token-per-second variant is the audio tokenizer of Apertus 1.5.
